news.title: A handheld gripper exposes the robot's movement limits during recording
news.summary: A University of Technology Nuremberg team and partners introduced RUMI for recording motion and contact data. In a small study, displaying the robot arm together with aligning its starting pose reduced recordings containing joint-limit violations.
news.details: Researchers from the University of Technology Nuremberg, Siemens and the Technical University of Munich posted RUMI on November 11, a study of a handheld device for recording robot demonstrations. Its gripper matches the geometry of the commercial Robotiq 2F-85, including the nonlinear relation between opening and finger movement. A person moves the device with an object while interchangeable fingertip sensors record contact information. A headset also displays the target robot arm's configuration, allowing the operator to compare the demonstrated motion with what that arm can execute.
news.technical_novelty: A University of Technology Nuremberg team and partners introduced RUMI for recording motion and contact data. In a small study, displaying the robot arm together with aligning its starting pose reduced recordings containing joint-limit violations. Five participants with limited experience of this form of control each recorded ten box transfers under two conditions. Joint-position limits were exceeded in 3 of 50 episodes with robot visualization and starting-pose alignment, compared with 16 of 50 without that assistance. The supported condition combined two features, so the comparison concerns their combined effect. A separate experiment examined force-aware demonstrations for moving a fragile bulb and a heavy block in simulation.
news.engineering_impact: A University of Technology Nuremberg team and partners introduced RUMI for recording motion and contact data. In a small study, displaying the robot arm together with aligning its starting pose reduced recordings containing joint-limit violations. The engineering problem arises before policy training: a person's demonstration must fit the target arm's kinematics. Matching the gripper geometry preserves how its fingers move, while displaying the arm makes joint constraints visible during recording. Separate physical experiments trained programs for gear assembly, wiping, screw tightening and box sorting. Different tasks used different fingertip sensors. Their outcomes therefore concern specific combinations of hardware, observations and operation, rather than a single aggregate measure of all demonstration quality. The team swapped fingertips between CoinFT, which measures forces and torques, and DIGIT, which images the contact surface.
news.limitations: A University of Technology Nuremberg team and partners introduced RUMI for recording motion and contact data. In a small study, displaying the robot arm together with aligning its starting pose reduced recordings containing joint-limit violations. The authors identify two device limits: only the wrist-camera viewpoint is available, and the squeeze-blocking mechanism does not reproduce external forces in every direction. Those properties define which contact information reaches the person recording the demonstration.
news.evidence_status: Author preprint with a small user study, separate physical-robot trials and a separate simulated contact experiment.
news.organization: University of Technology Nuremberg; Siemens; Technical University of Munich
news.body:
Researchers from the University of Technology Nuremberg, Siemens and the Technical University of Munich posted RUMI on November 11, a study of a handheld device for recording robot demonstrations. Its gripper matches the geometry of the commercial Robotiq 2F-85, including the nonlinear relation between opening and finger movement. A person moves the device with an object while interchangeable fingertip sensors record contact information. A headset also displays the target robot arm's configuration, allowing the operator to compare the demonstrated motion with what that arm can execute.

Five participants with limited experience of this form of control each recorded ten box transfers under two conditions. Joint-position limits were exceeded in 3 of 50 episodes with robot visualization and starting-pose alignment, compared with 16 of 50 without that assistance. The supported condition combined two features, so the comparison concerns their combined effect. A separate experiment examined force-aware demonstrations for moving a fragile bulb and a heavy block in simulation.

The engineering problem arises before policy training: a person's demonstration must fit the target arm's kinematics. Matching the gripper geometry preserves how its fingers move, while displaying the arm makes joint constraints visible during recording. Separate physical experiments trained programs for gear assembly, wiping, screw tightening and box sorting. Different tasks used different fingertip sensors. Their outcomes therefore concern specific combinations of hardware, observations and operation, rather than a single aggregate measure of all demonstration quality. The team swapped fingertips between CoinFT, which measures forces and torques, and DIGIT, which images the contact surface.

The authors identify two device limits: only the wrist-camera viewpoint is available, and the squeeze-blocking mechanism does not reproduce external forces in every direction. Those properties define which contact information reaches the person recording the demonstration.

news.title: XInfer schedules robot computation around feedback deadlines
news.summary: The X Square Robot team introduced a serving system for models that turn images and instructions into actions. Across three models, it supported more emulated robots under a specified median-response criterion.
news.details: The X Square Robot team introduced XInfer on November 11, a server system that shares computation across requests from multiple robots. It targets vision-language-action models, usually called VLA models, which turn images, a language instruction and machine state into actions. Image processing, context preparation and motion generation use computing resources differently. XInfer allows independent stages to overlap but postpones additional work when it would threaten another robot's response deadline. Priorities depend on the computation still required and the load already running on the processor.
news.technical_novelty: The X Square Robot team introduced a serving system for models that turn images and instructions into actions. Across three models, it supported more emulated robots under a specified median-response criterion. The authors compared three control models, VLA-2B, Wall-OSS-0.5 and π0.5, on consumer NVIDIA Blackwell graphics processors, keeping each model's inputs and computing settings fixed across serving systems. XInfer supported validated populations of 18, 15 and 24 emulated robots, against 11, 10 and 19 for a reimplementation of the Robion serving system. This comparison required no request errors and median response latency below 150 milliseconds in all three measurement windows. Image capture, input packing and parsing the returned answer are outside that latency measurement. A separate scheduling study uses a different criterion based on meeting individual response budgets.
news.engineering_impact: The X Square Robot team introduced a serving system for models that turn images and instructions into actions. Across three models, it supported more emulated robots under a specified median-response criterion. The important difference from an ordinary request queue is that latency matters differently across a movement. Transport can tolerate a different wait from precise alignment or contact. In a separate test, the authors alternated response budgets of 90 and 400 milliseconds. Requiring at least 95% of requests to meet their deadlines, XInfer supported 18 emulated robots. First-come-first-served scheduling reached 14, while scheduling by earliest deadline reached 12. These alternatives shared the same computing backend, making the scheduling policy the object of that comparison.
news.limitations: The X Square Robot team introduced a serving system for models that turn images and instructions into actions. Across three models, it supported more emulated robots under a specified median-response criterion. Server capacity depends on the criterion chosen. The three-model experiment uses median latency, whereas the varying-budget study measures the share of on-time answers. Results should be compared within their respective protocols, with the measurement boundary retained.
news.evidence_status: Author preprint and serving measurements using production-derived workloads; the capacity comparison uses emulated robot requests.
news.body:
The X Square Robot team introduced XInfer on November 11, a server system that shares computation across requests from multiple robots. It targets vision-language-action models, usually called VLA models, which turn images, a language instruction and machine state into actions. Image processing, context preparation and motion generation use computing resources differently. XInfer allows independent stages to overlap but postpones additional work when it would threaten another robot's response deadline. Priorities depend on the computation still required and the load already running on the processor.

The authors compared three control models, VLA-2B, Wall-OSS-0.5 and π0.5, on consumer NVIDIA Blackwell graphics processors, keeping each model's inputs and computing settings fixed across serving systems. XInfer supported validated populations of 18, 15 and 24 emulated robots, against 11, 10 and 19 for a reimplementation of the Robion serving system. This comparison required no request errors and median response latency below 150 milliseconds in all three measurement windows. Image capture, input packing and parsing the returned answer are outside that latency measurement. A separate scheduling study uses a different criterion based on meeting individual response budgets.

The important difference from an ordinary request queue is that latency matters differently across a movement. Transport can tolerate a different wait from precise alignment or contact. In a separate test, the authors alternated response budgets of 90 and 400 milliseconds. Requiring at least 95% of requests to meet their deadlines, XInfer supported 18 emulated robots. First-come-first-served scheduling reached 14, while scheduling by earliest deadline reached 12. These alternatives shared the same computing backend, making the scheduling policy the object of that comparison.

Server capacity depends on the criterion chosen. The three-model experiment uses median latency, whereas the varying-budget study measures the share of on-time answers. Results should be compared within their respective protocols, with the measurement boundary retained.

news.title: Komatsu trucks will connect autonomous driving with site dispatch
news.summary: Komatsu and TIER IV began developing autonomous systems for three dump-truck groups. The project includes both individual vehicle operations and integration with management of traffic across the worksite.
news.details: Komatsu and Japan's TIER IV announced joint development of autonomous control for three dump-truck groups on November 13. Deployment at quarry and civil-engineering sites in Japan and North America is targeted for 2027. The partners combine vehicle design and control with autonomous-driving technology. Development and validation will cover loading, hauling and dumping within actual site operations. A connection to the fleet-management system developed by Komatsu subsidiary EARTHBRAIN is intended to coordinate the wider worksite as well as individual vehicles.
news.technical_novelty: Komatsu and TIER IV began developing autonomous systems for three dump-truck groups. The project includes both individual vehicle operations and integration with management of traffic across the worksite. The program covers rigid-frame HD785 trucks with a maximum payload of 93.9 tonnes, HD605 trucks at 64.1 tonnes, and the articulated HM400/460 group at 42 tonnes. These are the vehicles’ rated payloads. Collaboration began in September 2025; the new announcement identifies specific machines and deployment settings for its next stage. The release shows an HD785 operating at a Komatsu test site. The companies plan to accumulate operating knowledge through trials and site introductions, connecting vehicle-level control with the organization of transport across a working location.
news.engineering_impact: Komatsu and TIER IV began developing autonomous systems for three dump-truck groups. The project includes both individual vehicle operations and integration with management of traffic across the worksite. The integration has two levels. On the vehicle, driving software must work with the machine's design and actuation controls. Across the site, loading, transport and dumping need coordination through the dispatch system. Choosing several truck platforms makes this a development program spanning different machines. The published plan includes loading and dumping in its operational validation scenarios. Those actions connect a vehicle's route to other participants in the production process, making the relationship between vehicle control and site organization a concrete part of the stated scope. Rigid-frame vehicles support the front and load sections on one frame; articulated vehicles have a joint between sections.
news.limitations: Komatsu and TIER IV began developing autonomous systems for three dump-truck groups. The project includes both individual vehicle operations and integration with management of traffic across the worksite. The announcement targets introduction in 2027 but does not provide autonomous productivity, operator-intervention or uninterrupted-operation measurements. Those results will need to be associated with a particular truck and the operating conditions of its site.
news.evidence_status: Official joint development and testing plan; vehicle specifications are company-reported.
news.body:
Komatsu and Japan's TIER IV announced joint development of autonomous control for three dump-truck groups on November 13. Deployment at quarry and civil-engineering sites in Japan and North America is targeted for 2027. The partners combine vehicle design and control with autonomous-driving technology. Development and validation will cover loading, hauling and dumping within actual site operations. A connection to the fleet-management system developed by Komatsu subsidiary EARTHBRAIN is intended to coordinate the wider worksite as well as individual vehicles.

The program covers rigid-frame HD785 trucks with a maximum payload of 93.9 tonnes, HD605 trucks at 64.1 tonnes, and the articulated HM400/460 group at 42 tonnes. These are the vehicles’ rated payloads. Collaboration began in September 2025; the new announcement identifies specific machines and deployment settings for its next stage. The release shows an HD785 operating at a Komatsu test site. The companies plan to accumulate operating knowledge through trials and site introductions, connecting vehicle-level control with the organization of transport across a working location.

The integration has two levels. On the vehicle, driving software must work with the machine's design and actuation controls. Across the site, loading, transport and dumping need coordination through the dispatch system. Choosing several truck platforms makes this a development program spanning different machines. The published plan includes loading and dumping in its operational validation scenarios. Those actions connect a vehicle's route to other participants in the production process, making the relationship between vehicle control and site organization a concrete part of the stated scope. Rigid-frame vehicles support the front and load sections on one frame; articulated vehicles have a joint between sections.

The announcement targets introduction in 2027 but does not provide autonomous productivity, operator-intervention or uninterrupted-operation measurements. Those results will need to be associated with a particular truck and the operating conditions of its site.

news.title: AWS survey links physical-AI scale-up to customers and production
news.summary: Amazon’s cloud-computing business AWS published a survey of 500 founders and executives building technologies for machine action in the real world. Among respondents with pilots, only 36% converted most or all into paid deployments.
news.details: Amazon Web Services, Amazon's cloud-computing business, published research on European physical-AI startups on November 14. Physical AI here covers technologies enabling machines to perceive and act in the real world. Strand Partners surveyed 500 founders and senior leaders for AWS in August. Fifty-one percent reported technology in commercial use, and 76% sell to large enterprises and industrial groups. The sample includes robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, control models and development tools, with several types of enabling technology represented.
news.technical_novelty: Amazon’s cloud-computing business AWS published a survey of 500 founders and executives building technologies for machine action in the real world. Among respondents with pilots, only 36% converted most or all into paid deployments. Among respondents who had run pilots, only 36% said most or all had become paid deployments. Slow enterprise purchasing was identified by 64%, while 59% described access to capital as a major challenge. These are answers to different survey questions; the pilot-conversion figure specifically concerns companies that had conducted pilots. AWS links further growth to manufacturing finance, customers willing to co-develop, technical skills and more consistent rules. The publication is new in November, while the opinions and business conditions measured by the survey date from August.
news.engineering_impact: Amazon’s cloud-computing business AWS published a survey of 500 founders and executives building technologies for machine action in the real world. Among respondents with pilots, only 36% converted most or all into paid deployments. For developers, a significant finding concerns the industrial customer. Companies already in deployment identified a customer willing to co-develop as the leading factor enabling deployment. Seventy-eight percent said proximity to European industrial customers helps them reach production faster. That highlights access to working conditions and feedback while adapting a system. The evidence is executives' assessment rather than an experiment measuring time saved. The sponsor also sells cloud infrastructure and promotes physical-AI development tools, which is part of the context in which the findings are published.
news.limitations: Amazon’s cloud-computing business AWS published a survey of 500 founders and executives building technologies for machine action in the real world. Among respondents with pilots, only 36% converted most or all into paid deployments. The sample excludes businesses that only use physical AI developed by others. It therefore describes technology builders. Its answer shares cannot be applied to industrial customers as a whole without a separate customer survey.
news.evidence_status: Executive survey commissioned by AWS and conducted by Strand Partners in August; findings published November 14.
news.body:
Amazon Web Services, Amazon's cloud-computing business, published research on European physical-AI startups on November 14. Physical AI here covers technologies enabling machines to perceive and act in the real world. Strand Partners surveyed 500 founders and senior leaders for AWS in August. Fifty-one percent reported technology in commercial use, and 76% sell to large enterprises and industrial groups. The sample includes robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, control models and development tools, with several types of enabling technology represented.

Among respondents who had run pilots, only 36% said most or all had become paid deployments. Slow enterprise purchasing was identified by 64%, while 59% described access to capital as a major challenge. These are answers to different survey questions; the pilot-conversion figure specifically concerns companies that had conducted pilots. AWS links further growth to manufacturing finance, customers willing to co-develop, technical skills and more consistent rules. The publication is new in November, while the opinions and business conditions measured by the survey date from August.

For developers, a significant finding concerns the industrial customer. Companies already in deployment identified a customer willing to co-develop as the leading factor enabling deployment. Seventy-eight percent said proximity to European industrial customers helps them reach production faster. That highlights access to working conditions and feedback while adapting a system. The evidence is executives' assessment rather than an experiment measuring time saved. The sponsor also sells cloud infrastructure and promotes physical-AI development tools, which is part of the context in which the findings are published.

The sample excludes businesses that only use physical AI developed by others. It therefore describes technology builders. Its answer shares cannot be applied to industrial customers as a whole without a separate customer survey.

news.title: Bessent asks NVIDIA for answers on export controls
news.summary: The U.S. Treasury secretary called on NVIDIA's board and outside counsel to answer within ten days on November 15. He also urged an external permanent chief executive, while the company's announced search still includes internal candidates.
news.details: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged NVIDIA to recruit its next chief executive from outside the company on November 15. He also called for answers from its board and outside counsel within ten days about compliance with export restrictions. He spoke on Sunday Morning Futures, and Reuters independently reported the remarks. The new development is public pressure on the succession process and controls over chip sales. His allegations about possible compliance failures remain attributed to him; the report does not present findings from a completed investigation.
news.technical_novelty: The U.S. Treasury secretary called on NVIDIA's board and outside counsel to answer within ten days on November 15. He also urged an external permanent chief executive, while the company's announced search still includes internal candidates. The company-confirmed leadership position is that Jensen Huang left his roles as president, chief executive and director, with chief financial officer Colette Kress becoming interim chief executive. In its November 12 announcement, the board said it would consider internal and external candidates and expected operations, customer commitments and product plans to continue. Financial results are scheduled for November 17. Bessent's proposal therefore calls for a narrower candidate pool than the board's previously announced process. The checked reports do not name a permanent appointment resulting from Sunday's intervention.
news.engineering_impact: The U.S. Treasury secretary called on NVIDIA's board and outside counsel to answer within ten days on November 15. He also urged an external permanent chief executive, while the company's announced search still includes internal candidates. For teams using NVIDIA computing platforms, the intervention concerns supplier governance and controls over international sales. Its technical effect has not been measured. The company's stated position remains the board's commitment to continue product plans and customer obligations. Assessing dependencies therefore requires distinguishing that published supplier commitment from a government official's demand to alter the leadership search. The latter adds a new management question, but it does not supply an announced schedule of changes to software libraries, boards or simulation tools used by robotics teams.
news.limitations: The U.S. Treasury secretary called on NVIDIA's board and outside counsel to answer within ten days on November 15. He also urged an external permanent chief executive, while the company's announced search still includes internal candidates. The ten days are the response period Bessent named on television. The checked material does not establish a court order or a newly enacted export rule. The content of the requested answers is still unknown.
news.evidence_status: Bessent’s public remarks checked against FOX Business and Reuters; leadership status confirmed by NVIDIA’s announcement.
news.organization: U.S. Department of the Treasury; NVIDIA

Financial results are scheduled for November 17. Bessent's proposal therefore calls for a narrower candidate pool than the board's previously announced process. The checked reports do not name a permanent appointment resulting from Sunday's intervention.

For teams using NVIDIA computing platforms, the intervention concerns supplier governance and controls over international sales. Its technical effect has not been measured.
